notes: The oldest open transaction (connection 93, 20 min 50 s) runs under REPEATABLE READ, so after its first consistent read it keeps a read view until it ends: InnoDB cannot purge the undo logs that view may still need, and the history list length grows.
Statuses are rules of thumb, not verdicts. The summary counts every session this account can see; the filters narrow only the list. This tool's own session is left out.

rules.connections: watch at 75% of max_connections, problem at 90% (Threads_connected)
rules.idle_in_trx: a session idle (Sleep) inside an open InnoDB transaction keeps its row locks; under REPEATABLE READ it also keeps the read view from its first consistent read, which holds back purge; watched when the transaction is 10 s old, a problem at 60 s (rules of thumb)
rules.lock_wait: a session waiting for an InnoDB lock (INNODB_TRX trx_state LOCK WAIT: a row lock or an InnoDB table lock such as AUTO-INC), a metadata lock, or a table-level lock is watched; the long-running rule raises it to a problem
rules.long_running: a statement running for 10 s or more is watched, 60 s or more is a problem (rules of thumb for OLTP; reports and batch jobs can run longer by design)
rules.oldest_transaction: the oldest open transaction is watched at 10 s and a problem at 60 s; under REPEATABLE READ (or while a statement runs) its read view also holds back purge, so the history list length grows behind it

history_list_length.rule: a rule of thumb without a trend: watch at 100,000 committed transactions whose undo logs purge has not processed yet, problem at 1,000,000. The size alone says little; a list that keeps growing across refreshes means purge is falling behind, most often because an old read view (a REPEATABLE READ transaction or a long statement) is still open
